county_referendums.title: Renewal of the 5th and 6th Cent Local Option Fuel Tax
county_referendums.ballot_question: Sumter County currently levies a 5th and 6th cent local option fuel tax generating an estimated $2,648,888 in annual revenue to fund road maintenance, road construction, and other transportation infrastructure. Fuel taxes are proportionately shared, based on population, with cities within the county. Shall Sumter County continue to levy a 5th and 6th cent tax per gallon on motor fuel sold within the county, for a period up to 30 years beginning January 1, 2028?
county_referendums.what_yes_means: A YES vote continues the existing two cents per gallon (the '5th and 6th cent') of local option fuel tax on gasoline and diesel sold in Sumter County for up to 30 more years, through 2057, after the current levy expires Dec. 31, 2027. The county says the tax raised slightly over $2 million in 2024 and is dedicated to road resurfacing, construction, bridge work and pavement markings, with about 89% retained by the county and the rest shared with cities by population.
county_referendums.what_no_means: A NO vote lets the two-cent levy expire on Dec. 31, 2027, reducing the local fuel tax from eight cents to six cents per gallon and removing roughly $2-2.6 million a year that the county now spends on roads; the county would have to fund those projects from other sources or reduce them.
county_referendums.background: Sumter County adopted the levy by ordinance in March 2008 and extended it in 2020 through 2027. Florida law requires voter approval to continue the 5th and 6th cent tax beyond its expiration, and the County Commission voted to place the renewal on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot. The county launched a 'Your Fuel Taxes At Work' information campaign; County Administrator Bradley Arnold said 'a dependable transportation network is essential to emergency response, commerce, and daily life.' No organized opposition was found in the sources reviewed.

county_referendums.title: Tourist Development Tax Ordinance
county_referendums.ballot_question: The levy and imposition of a 2% tourist development tax as set forth in Sumter County Ordinance 26-08 is subject to approval by the electors of Sumter County in a referendum election which is hereby scheduled for the General Election of 2026 which is to be held on November 3, 2026.
county_referendums.choices: FOR the Tourist Development Tax / AGAINST the Tourist Development Tax
county_referendums.what_yes_means: A vote FOR approves a 2% tax on short-term lodging (hotels, motels, campgrounds, vacation rentals and similar stays of six months or less) in Sumter County under Ordinance 26-08. Villages-News reported the tax is expected to raise about $1 million a year, to be spent on tourism-related purposes allowed by state law such as fairgrounds improvements and entertainment at The Villages town squares, with a Tourist Development Council advising the county.
county_referendums.what_no_means: A vote AGAINST means no tourist development tax is levied; Sumter County would remain without a 'bed tax' (the commission suspended its earlier levy in October 2020).
county_referendums.background: In May 2026 the County Commission approved an ordinance creating a Tourist Development Council as the first step toward reviving the tax and set the referendum for Nov. 3. Commissioner Deb Butterfield supported it, saying tourists rather than residents pay it and 'we're leaving precious money on the table'; Chairman Don Wiley voted for the ordinance but said it 'puts an additional tax burden on our businesses' and questioned whether short-term rentals in The Villages would comply. Renters of homes for six months or less would also pay the tax.
